comparison: Both address phenotypic characterization claims (C22-C24). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with appropriate validation. Peer review raises significant concerns about ovulation data inconsistency with literature and questions follicle counting methodology, marking it UNCERTAIN versus OpenEval's SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate MIMS data on macromolecular longevity (C25-C29). OpenEval finds claims supported with caveat about 'limited turnover' inference. Peer review explicitly states enrichment of LLPs is 'soundly supported' and provides 'convincing evidence,' both marking SUPPORTED, though peer review groups with C30-C32.

OpenEval evaluates differential LLP distribution in somatic compartments (C30-C32) as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups these claims with C25-C29 and finds the overall enrichment pattern 'soundly supported,' both agreeing on SUPPORTED status.

OpenEval marks claims C33-C34 about nuclear signal interpretation as UNCERTAIN due to MIMS limitations in distinguishing protein-bound vs nucleic acid-bound nitrogen. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific speculative claims.
OpenEval finds summary conclusions C35-C36 SUPPORTED based on persistence of 15N signal and aging phenotype data. No specific peer review evaluation addresses these integrative summary claims.

Both evaluate LC-MS/MS protein identification data (C37-C41). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with caveat about technical limitations. Peer review states GO enrichment claims are 'well supported' and describes as 'helpful data about protein turnover,' both agreeing on SUPPORTED status.

OpenEval evaluates fractional abundance data showing gradual turnover (C42-C43) as SUPPORTED with cautious interpretation. Peer review groups with broader LC-MS/MS findings and notes timepoint differences as 'striking' strength, both marking SUPPORTED.

Both address ZP3 as LLP finding (C44, C46). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED and notes it as novel/unexpected. Peer review highlights it as 'interesting findings' worthy of follow-up with no challenges, both marking SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate protein turnover evidence (C48-C50). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with technical caveats. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN - while accepting descriptive findings, Reviewer 2 questions verification and notes study is 'pretty descriptive' lacking functional validation.

OpenEval evaluates GO analysis (C51) as SUPPORTED with caveat about reference proteome. Peer review groups with broader findings (C48-C51, C57-C61) and while Reviewer 1 accepts GO claims as 'well supported,' Reviewer 2's concerns about verification lead to UNCERTAIN overall.

OpenEval finds fractional abundance data at 10 months (C52-C54) SUPPORTED, with reasonable interpretation about selective retention. No specific peer review evaluation addresses these temporal FA comparison claims.

OpenEval evaluates mitochondrial protein data (C55-C56) as SUPPORTED, noting important distinction between total and long-lived protein abundance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mitochondrial claims.

OpenEval evaluates hierarchical clustering and differential longevity (C57-C61) as SUPPORTED with robust evidence. Peer review groups with C48-C51 and marks UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 2's concerns about verification despite Reviewer 1 accepting GO enrichment as 'well supported.'

Both evaluate cross-tissue comparison claims (C62-C67). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with reasonable inference about tissue-specific functions. Peer review explicitly states this represents 'first study' on ovarian LLP turnover and is 'important,' both marking SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate integration of MIMS data with follicle development (C68-C75). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with C75 noted as speculative but reasonable. Peer review states claims are 'soundly supported by analyses' with mechanistic interpretation accepted, both marking SUPPORTED.

Both address OSE findings and DNA segregation hypothesis (C76-C80). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN due to C80 being highly speculative without direct proof. Peer review marks SUPPORTED, highlighting 'surprising' OSE enrichment as worthy of follow-up and accepting speculative interpretation as hypothesis-generating.

Both evaluate ZP3 interpretations and alternative hypotheses (C85-C91). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED noting sound logic though mechanism uncertain. Peer review marks SUPPORTED, specifically mentioning ZP3 raises 'important unanswered questions worthy of follow-up' and accepting hypothesis-generating nature.

Both evaluate temporal analysis connecting protein turnover to aging (C92-C97). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with caveat that causal relationship needs establishment. Peer review marks SUPPORTED, noting timepoint differences as 'striking' and 'most striking' strength providing 'helpful data about protein turnover.'

Both address tubulin findings and implications (C98-C102). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with speculative but reasonable hypotheses. Peer review marks SUPPORTED, highlighting 'Tubb family proteins' as 'interesting findings' worthy of follow-up within hypothesis-generating framework.

OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of MS technical limitations (C103-C104) as SUPPORTED, noting honest assessment. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this methodological limitation discussion.

Both evaluate histone turnover interpretation (C105-C106). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation about dynamic turnover. Peer review marks SUPPORTED, noting interpretation is based on cited literature and consistent with data, not challenged by reviewers.

Both evaluate actin longevity and protective function hypothesis (C107-C110). OpenEval marks SUPPORTED with C110 noted as speculative requiring validation. Peer review marks SUPPORTED, noting work 'will contribute to hypothesis generation' and accepting speculative protective role as appropriately presented.

OpenEval evaluates mitochondrial LLP dynamics (C111-C120) as SUPPORTED with compelling spatial-temporal integration. Peer review (R15) addresses subset (C112-C117) as SUPPORTED, noting findings 'well described within known body of evidence.' Peer review R10 addresses C118-C120, C122 as SUPPORTED for hypothesis generation.

Both address transgenerational effects hypothesis (C122). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN noting speculation lacks direct experimental evidence. Peer review marks SUPPORTED within hypothesis-generating framework, noting speculative interpretations are presented appropriately and not challenged.
